name: tiermux
description: Free agentic AI coding assistant for VS Code. Multiplexes many free-tier LLM providers into one self-healing surface — auto-routes, auto-fails-over, learns your codebase. Zero setup with keyless providers; bring your own keys anytime.

tiermux.agent.pruneAtTokens.description: During a long agent turn, once the running context passes this many tokens, older tool outputs and reasoning are pruned before each step so the model stops re-sending stale grep/read dumps. Lower = leaner context (cheaper, better for small free-tier windows); 0 disables pruning. When left at the default (not explicitly set), this scales automatically with the routed model's context window (40% of the window, clamped 12k–60k) — set a value here to override the adaptive behavior.

tiermux.agent.maxStepsPerTurn.description: Hard ceiling on the number of tool-loop steps in a SINGLE agent turn (0 = no limit). A backstop for the one runaway shape the other brakes miss: many distinct mutating tool calls (none exact-repeating, all 'real progress') that nonetheless sprawl. Fires as a budget-style cutoff (bounded by maxBudgetContinuations), not a resumable pause. Default 50: a legit task rarely exceeds 50 steps in one turn — long tasks span auto-continue rounds instead.

tiermux.agent.maxConcurrentRuns.description: Maximum number of chat sessions that run their agent at the same time. Extra sends queue and start as a slot frees, to respect free-tier rate limits.

tiermux.agent.requireWriteConfirmation.description: Show a diff and ask for confirmation before the agent writes/creates/deletes a file.

tiermux.agent.smartScoring.description: Route Auto requests by learned, per-model runtime metrics (success rate, TTFT vs the model's own baseline, provider health, confidence-weighted) instead of fixed priority. Adapts within minutes when a model or gateway degrades. Turn off to restore priority-only routing.

tiermux.agent.verifyCommand.description: Command run automatically after a turn edits files, to verify the project still works (a non-zero exit triggers bounded fix-and-recheck rounds). 'auto' detects it from the project (package.json test/typecheck/lint/build script, Makefile check/test, cargo test, go test, pytest, composer test); the planner's 'Verify:' line overrides per task; any other value is used verbatim; 'off' disables.

tiermux.agent.verifyFixRounds.description: When the verify command fails after a turn edits files, the failure output is fed back to the agent for up to this many fix-and-recheck rounds before the turn reports failure. The agent owns the recheck — no manual re-run needed. 0 disables (the failure is reported as-is).

tiermux.agent.reanchorChars.description: Late re-anchoring: after stale read results are pruned from a long turn, re-show up to this many characters of the files the model actually read, so it answers about code it can still see rather than from memory. 0 disables. Weak models benefit most — reasoning errors concentrate late in a turn, which is exactly when pruning has removed the evidence.

tiermux.agent.toolCompaction.description: Compact bulky tool results before they enter the model's context: 'light' keeps only the head and tail of large runCommand outputs (the model keeps the outcome and final status); 'aggressive' additionally line-caps search-shaped results (grep/glob/listDir/webSearch). File reads, edit results, and diagnostics are never compacted. 'off' keeps every result verbatim.

tiermux.profiler.enabled.description: Collect per-turn performance traces (latency, tokens, fallbacks) into an in-memory ring buffer, viewable from the TierMux profiler command.

tiermux.profiler.ringSize.description: Maximum number of recent turns the profiler keeps in its ring buffer.

tiermux.agent.autoCondense.description: Automatically compact the conversation (summarize older turns) when its history approaches ~80% of the routed model's context window, before a turn starts — so the model begins with headroom instead of losing tool evidence to mid-turn pruning. The manual Compact command still works regardless.

tiermux.agent.autoCondenseTokenCap.description: Absolute token ceiling for auto-compact targeting, even when the routed model advertises a larger context window. 0 disables the cap (window-only sizing).

tiermux.agent.sessionModelLock.description: Keep one conversation on the model that has been serving it successfully (continuity), instead of letting Auto re-pick every turn. The lock releases automatically on real failure — rate limits, errors, or the model being flagged slow — so failover is never blocked.

tiermux.agent.scoringTrace.description: Log the per-turn Smart Auto scoring rationale (why each model was selected or skipped, with per-signal scores) to the "TierMux Router" output channel.

tiermux.agent.diagTrace.description: Log the model's path from picker → router → provider → AI SDK (pinned value, resolved candidate, runtimeName, raw usage) to the "TierMux Diag" output channel. Temporary diagnostic for the wrong-provider-name / 0-token issue.

enumDescriptions: Ask for approval before every command (safest).
Auto-run a small set of safe inspection/test/build commands; ask for anything else.
tiermux.agent.commandApproval.description: How the agent's runCommand tool is gated before running shell commands.

tiermux.agent.commandTimeoutMs.description: Maximum time (ms) a single agent command may run before it is killed.

tiermux.agent.commandAllowlist.description: Extra command prefixes auto-runnable in 'allowlist' mode (e.g. "php artisan migrate"), in addition to the built-in safe defaults.

tiermux.agent.autoCompactThreshold.description: Automatically summarize (compact) the conversation when it exceeds this fraction of the model's context window. 0 disables auto-compact.

tiermux.index.enabled.description: Maintain an in-memory symbol + dependency index so the agent can look up definitions and import graphs directly instead of grepping.

tiermux.index.maxFiles.description: Maximum number of files the in-memory index will hold (bounds memory). Files beyond this are not indexed until older ones drop.

tiermux.index.excludes.description: Path segments/globs never indexed (e.g. "node_modules", "vendor", "*.min.js"). Empty uses the built-in defaults (node_modules, .git, dist, build, vendor, .next, out, coverage, .cache).

tiermux.graph.enabled.description: Offer the structural code-graph tools (getSymbolGraph, getDependencyTree) to the agent, giving it cross-file context from imports, exports, and call edges. Turn off to drop both tools from every turn — useful on a very large codebase, where the regex-based graph gets imprecise and the tool descriptions still cost prompt tokens.

tiermux.context.includeOpenEditors.description: Each turn, silently attach the active editor (the selection, or a slice around the cursor — see ambientSliceRadius) and its live diagnostics to the model-facing prompt. The visible transcript is unchanged; this just lets "fix this" resolve to the cursor location.

tiermux.context.ambientSliceRadius.description: Lines of context on each side of the cursor to include with the active file. Lower = fewer tokens per turn (helps free-tier quotas).

tiermux.utilityModel.description: Model used for short utility tasks (chat titles, commit messages). 'auto' prefers a strong keyless model so it works without an API key; or pick a specific model in Settings → Others.

tiermux.classifierModel.description: Model the task classifier (Auto routing) uses to decide what kind of request each message is. 'auto' prefers keyless models in order: OpenCode, Kilo Code, OVH. Or pin a specific model as platform::modelId (e.g. opencode::deepseek-v4-flash-free). If unavailable, the built-in regex classifier is used instead.

tiermux.plan.saveToFile.description: Save actionable plans proposed in Plan mode as markdown checklist files you can read and edit. The plan and its live task checklist are also shown in chat.

tiermux.plan.folder.description: Workspace-relative folder where plan files are written (one markdown file per plan).

tiermux.requestTimeoutMs.description: Per-provider request timeout (ms) before failing over to the next model. Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints and pinned (non-Auto) models run uncapped — you chose to wait for that model, and the Stop button is the brake.

tiermux.ttftTimeoutMs.description: Time-to-first-token fast failover (lightweight hedging) for streaming requests. If a model accepts the connection but emits no chunk within this many ms, abort it and fail over to the next candidate instead of waiting the full requestTimeoutMs. Catches models that pass preflight then hang mid-stream — the case the ping can't detect. Any first chunk (content, reasoning, or keepalive) clears the timer. 0 disables. Clamped to requestTimeoutMs. Custom OpenAI-compatible endpoints have the gate disabled entirely (local models need their load + prefill time before the first token, and no cloud pool can serve that model faster). Pinned (non-Auto) models also skip the gate — there is nothing to fail over to, so waiting is the only honest option.

tiermux.rateLimitCooldownMs.description: How long (ms) to skip a rate-limited provider before trying it again. Honors a provider's Retry-After header when present.

tiermux.hedging.description: Delayed request hedging for streaming turns: if the chosen model produces no chunk at all within tiermux.hedgeDelayMs, start the next candidate concurrently and keep whichever responds first (the other is aborted). The hedge never fires when the primary is healthy, so token cost is unchanged in the common case — it only converts 'waited out a slow model' into 'waited ~2.5s'.

tiermux.hedgeDelayMs.description: How long (ms) to wait for the first provider chunk before starting a hedge request alongside the primary. 0 disables hedging (same as tiermux.hedging: false). Clamped below tiermux.ttftTimeoutMs.

tiermux.completions.enabled.description: Enable Copilot-style inline (ghost-text) completions. Off by default — high request volume against free-tier rate limits.

tiermux.completions.model.description: Model id used for inline completions, or 'auto' to use a fast enabled model.

tiermux.completions.debounceMs.description: Debounce (ms) before requesting an inline completion.

tiermux.catalog.url.description: URL that supplies the model catalog. Accepts the TierMux worker JSON ({ providers: [{ provider_id, enabled, models: [...] }] }) or a legacy published-sheet CSV. Fetched in the background when the editor starts; the last fetch is cached and used offline, falling back to the built-in catalog. Leave blank to use only the built-in catalog.

tiermux.mcpRegistryUrl.description: Optional URL to a custom curated MCP list (JSON array or {servers:[…]} in this extension's format). When set, it replaces the bundled 'Add a server' list shown when the search box is empty.

tiermux.mcpRegistrySearchUrl.description: Base URL of the MCP registry queried by the remote search box in the MCP panel (official MCP registry by default). Blank disables remote search.

command.description: stdio: executable to launch (e.g. npx, uvx, node).

cwd.description: stdio: working directory (defaults to the workspace root).

tiermux.profiler.enabled.description: Collect per-turn performance traces for diagnostics. Shows model latency, tool calls, TTFT, fallback rate, and quality gate triggers. Use 'TierMux: Show Profiler' to view.

tiermux.profiler.ringSize.description: Number of recent turns to keep in the profiler ring buffer.

tiermux.models.autoEnableNew.description: Automatically enable models newly discovered in the catalog. Models on providers you haven't enabled stay inactive regardless. Turn off to review each new model manually.

tiermux.fleet.maxWorkers.description: Maximum number of worker sub-agents the parallel pipeline (implementPipeline) runs at once. Each worker is a full router-routed loop, so raising this increases token cost (~N×) and rate-limit contention on shared providers.

tiermux.fleet.workerMaxSteps.description: Hard ceiling on the tool-loop step count for a single pipeline worker (the explore sub-agent uses 6; workers need more because they actually edit files).

tiermux.fleet.workerTimeoutMs.description: Wall-clock timeout (ms) for a single pipeline worker. On timeout the worker aborts and its branch is left for inspection; the parent turn's Stop button also aborts all workers.

tiermux.fleet.researchMaxSteps.description: Hard ceiling on the tool-loop step count for the research sub-agent (delegate mode "research"). Bigger than explore's quick lookup (6) but still cheap — it runs on a utility model with read-only tools.

tiermux.fleet.researchTimeoutMs.description: Wall-clock timeout (ms) for the research sub-agent. Also network-hang protection for slow or stuck free-tier providers, so prefer raising it over disabling it.

tiermux.fleet.stagingBranchPrefix.description: Prefix for the staging branch the pipeline merges worker branches into (e.g. tiermux/pipeline-<runId>). The user's working tree is never modified; you merge the staging branch into your own branch manually.

scripts.build: npm run sync:all && node esbuild.js --production && npm run build:types
scripts.sync:all: npm run sync:catalog && npm run sync:providers && npm run sync:readme
